question: Should exec denylist policy have one canonical persisted owner, or remain a union of openclaw.json and exec-approvals.json?
rationale: The final authorization receives forwarded config rules while the companion separately owns its approvals file; safe revocation, UI ownership, and upgrade semantics require explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: One canonical owner
options.body: Persist denylist policy in one store and migrate or derive the secondary representation.

options.title: Dual owners with locked union
options.body: Keep both stores only if every host re-resolves the complete union at final commit and maintainers approve the upgrade and UI contract.

recommendation.title: One canonical owner
recommendation.body: Persist denylist policy in one store and migrate or derive the secondary representation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history and adjacent merged work point to this person for the exec-approval security-boundary decision.
